findings.claim: AC-4 defines 'no field option' as none of the options being present, but the test plan never checks an empty-string option (--title '' or --due ''), so a build that tests truthiness instead of presence passes.
findings.failure_scenario: A build treats `edit 1 --title ''` as no field and prints 'nothing to edit' (or treats --due '' as absent) instead of the required blank-title / invalid due date error; both exit 2, so the only visible difference is the stderr text, which no test checks for the empty string.
findings.rule: AC-1, AC-4 (request: a blank title is refused; every value validated)
findings.evidence: `edit` with no field option (none of --title, --due, --no-due, --priority) exits 2 with one `error: ...` line on stderr and changes nothing.

defenses.quote: "edit 1 --title '   '" -> exit 2, stderr exactly 'error: title must not be empty', file unchanged.
defenses.reason: The test plan for AC-1 tests whitespace-only title ('   ') but not empty string (''), and the test plan for AC-4 tests no options but not empty options. An implementation using truthiness checks (if args.title:) instead of presence checks (if args.title is not None:) would treat empty strings as 'no field option' and pass the tests, violating AC-1's requirement to handle 'blank/whitespace-only title'. This is a valid gap in test coverage, though the acceptance criteria themselves are reasonably clear.
